relevance_note: The paper describes three individually tabulated patients with histologically proved Alexander disease ("three patients in whom the diagnosis of Alexander disease had already been proved histologically"), one column each in Table 2; no GFAP variant is mentioned anywhere in the text.
method_note: The Markdown is incomplete: no author/year header, abstract, introduction or methods, and the Results text is cut mid-sentence ('the distribution and extent Note.-'), so first_author and year are not reported. Scope: Table 2 has patients as columns (headers: 'Infantile Variant - Early MR', 'Infantile Variant - Late MR', 'Juvenile Variant - Early MR', 'Juvenile Variant - Late MR'), each with 'No. of patients' = 1. The text says there were three histologically proved patients and that 'the patient with juvenile Alexander disease' had three MR studies, one early and two late; columns 3 and 4 are therefore one person, labelled 'Table 2 column 3' (that person's late-MR data are in column 4), and columns 1 and 2 are taken to be two different infantile patients (3 patients minus the 1 juvenile patient; each column has 1 MR study). This two-patient reading of the infantile columns is an inference from the counts, not stated in so many words. The 19 patients with an MR imaging-based (presumed) diagnosis from the cohort of 217 are described only at group level (Tables 3 and 4 are counts for 5 and 14 patients); the scattered single-patient mentions ('A brain biopsy was performed in one patient', 'One patient received contrast material', the patients in Figs 4-6 at 4, 12 and 10 years) cannot be told apart and may overlap, so they got no rows to avoid inventing or merging people. Previously published cases (e.g. Gingold et al (32)) are mentioned without individual-level facts about an identified person; no rows. No GFAP variant, gene or genetic test is mentioned, so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported is null; cohort_size_as_stated is the 217 children screened (the 3 histologically proved patients are additional). Table 2 values: its legend says 'Numbers indicate the number of patients in whom a particular feature was observed'; with one patient per column, '1' was recorded as observed for that patient. A '0' is a count of zero and was not used to exclude anything (v4 zero-count rule); 'n.e.' (not evaluable) and 'n.c.' (no contrast given) are not reported. The Markdown flattens the table's hierarchy; sub-rows are recorded with their nearest preceding heading row (e.g. 'Involvement of deep nuclei: Caudate nucleus', 'Contrast enhancement: Frontal white matter') and that heading quoted as a second span. The sub-rows directly under 'Frontal predominance wma' (Extent of wma, Swelling wma, Degree of cystic degeneration, Degree of signal change, Width of periventricular rim and the first 'Contrast enhancement' row) appear to grade frontal predominance and were not recorded as separate features because their meaning is ambiguous in the flattened table; the first 'Contrast enhancement' row reads 0/1 for the juvenile early MR while the later 'Contrast enhancement' row reads 1 (possible inconsistency or different meaning; only the later row was used, and the 0/1 was not used to exclude). Ages at MR imaging (4 mo, 7 mo, 20 mo, '6 and 9 y') were not recorded as onset or last-evaluation ages. No clinical features are given per patient for these three, so clinical checklist items are not reported. Spans for Table 2 were cut from the table lines by a short script (row start through the patient's cell) and checked against the table; all values were chosen by reading the table.
